name: Hashabnah
title: Levite and Covenant Maker
summary: Hashabnah was a Levite or leader mentioned in the book of Nehemiah in connection with the renewal of the covenant after returning from exile in Babylon. He was among those who sealed the covenant with God and participated in the public confession and praise. His name appears several times in Nehemiah, possibly referring to more than one person with the same name.

keyEvents.title: Participation in Public Prayer and Confession
keyEvents.description: Hashabnah was among the Levites who cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God during a public service of repentance and prayer after the people had heard the words of the law.

keyEvents.title: Praise and Prayer to God
keyEvents.description: During the great prayer in Nehemiah 9, the Levites, including Hashabnah, led the people in a long prayer that reviewed God's faithfulness throughout Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: Sealing of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Hashabnah was among the Levitical leaders who put their seal on the written covenant to follow God's law, which Nehemiah initiated.

keyEvents.title: Covenant Obligations
keyEvents.description: By sealing the covenant, Hashabnah and the others committed themselves to keeping God's commands, statutes, and laws, including the Sabbath commandment and the temple tax.

keyEvents.title: Service among the Levites in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Hashabnah is also mentioned in connection with the organization of the Levites' service in rebuilt Jerusalem, where he played a leading role among the Levites.
